scope: Residual edge cases from the German and Italian Ottoman honour lists checked against TDV and focused academic sources

entries.decision: Retain in the historical commemorative appendix. The City of London/British issue commemorated the Sultan's visit but was not an Ottoman state award.
entries.evidence: Academic description identifies a 76.4 mm, 275.42 g bronze medal by J. S. and A. B. Wyon; auction references describe an original cased example and a mintage of 350.

entries.candidate: Sanay-i Nefise Madalyası / Medal of Fine Arts
entries.decision: Do not create a second family. A 2026 Belleten study states that the existing Sanayi medal was later transformed/renamed as Sanayi-i Nefise; the Italian list's 1889 label and Künker's 1884 fourth-model date are retained as period/date candidates until the regulation and object types are aligned.

entries.candidate: Ertuğrul, Meziyet and Ziraat Liyakat orders
entries.decision: Retain as three separate proposed/unmade schemes, outside the issued formal-family count. TDV says Ertuğrul was abandoned after its regulation and the other two were apparently not manufactured.

entries.candidate: Çelenk, sorguç, tuğ and pre-order robes or gifts
entries.decision: Do not merge ceremonial gifts, rank emblems, copies or horse-tail standards into medal/order counts. Çelenk remains a historical honour type; the current local example is explicitly a copy. A separate early-honours appendix requires object-level evidence.

The German list alone does not establish it as an Ottoman state decoration. Keep it out of the formal count pending an object page or regulation; if verified, place it with qualification/campaign badges rather than medals.
